summary: Observation of a luminous object with changes in direction.
description: On December 26, 1978, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness observed a luminous object moving across the sky. Passing through a cloud, this object emitted a luminous phenomenon and ascended rapidly, turning red. The witness then saw only a red dot disappear. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation of the particular evolutions of a point of light in the sky: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony from 2016 of an earlier observation (date uncertain). On December 28, 1978, between 9 and 10 PM, three people observed a bright point of light moving across the sky for 20 to 30 minutes, following an irregular and angular trajectory. Changes in direction were perceived and appeared random. The witnesses left the terrace while the UFO was still moving. Only one witness statement was recorded. The description could correspond to an aircraft (civilian or otherwise) indeed following an unusual trajectory, which cannot be ruled out (we lack the resources to investigate such ancient air traffic), but it could also be a satellite. In fact, GEIPAN has experience with anomalies caused by satellites whose trajectories are not straight. The unusual appearance is due either to perceptual effects (see the article on the autokinetic effect) for the zigzags, or to the coincidence of a trajectory at the end of sunlight with another trajectory at the beginning of sunlight, giving the impression of a single satellite with a significant change in trajectory. The age of the observation and the lack of tools and databases dating back to that time prevent us from drawing conclusions in this case. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of the fall of a man-made object.
description: On December 25, 1978, at approximately 4:30 PM, three people observed a smooth, luminous, spherical or oval object, over one meter in diameter, falling to the ground. This multicolored sphere caught fire upon impact. The police investigation found traces of charred earth and various fragments at the crash site (a spring, an aluminum plate, rolled and broken electrical tape). The nature of the debris collected at the crash site clearly indicated a man-made device, although its exact nature (a gondola, a balloon, a kite) could not be determined. It was likely an amateur experiment.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous object.
description: On December 24, 1978, at approximately 9:00 PM, two witnesses observed a luminous object in the sky. They noted the object's slow movement and the emitting of various colors. Around 11:00 PM, one of the witnesses confirmed seeing the object again, which had once more changed position. No further testimony corroborated these very brief accounts.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of two objects in the sky.
description: On December 20, 1978, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness observed long pink trails in the sky, followed by two spinning, top-shaped objects. During the objects' very high-speed movement, the primary witness heard no noise. Another witness called to the scene saw only a blaze in the sky. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Long observations of a bright point in the sky: observations of Venus.
description: On Tuesday, December 19, 1978, at 8:23 a.m., a witness on his balcony observed a phenomenon he did not recognize. In the clear sky to the southeast of Meaux, a bright point of light was moving. The object disappeared around 9:45 a.m., hidden by the sun. From the apartment, gendarmes also observed a bright point of light in the same direction at an altitude of approximately 35°. The previous day in Paris, two witnesses were intrigued by the presence of a particularly bright object in the sky, and a police team also noted its presence. The Parisian police investigation concluded that it was an astronomical observation. Astronomical verification (see star chart) clearly indicated Venus was located between 25° and 30° to the southeast at the time indicated. GEIPAN classified this case as "A": astronomical misidentification of Venus.

summary: Observations of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 11, 1978, witnesses in several departments observed a luminous phenomenon moving rapidly across the sky without any sound being heard. A trail was also seen. This phenomenon disappeared suddenly. These people likely observed atmospheric reentry.

summary: Astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On December 10, 1978, starting at 6:40 a.m., several witnesses, including police officers, observed a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the western sky. This phenomenon appeared to have a pendulum-like, upward motion. It gradually diminished and disappeared around 9:30 a.m. These witnesses observed the planet Venus.

summary: Probable aircraft sighting.
description: During a Rome-Paris flight, a passenger observed a bright, elongated object moving from right to left beneath the aircraft. The pilot, questioned upon arrival, recalled seeing a bright aircraft in the setting sun, moving from right to left, at the time indicated by the passenger. This aircraft left a faint condensation trail behind it. The witness likely saw this aircraft.

summary: Successive observations of a luminous phenomenon.
description: Between December 6 and 9, 1978, a witness observed a luminous shape moving very slowly from east to south while returning home from work. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a round, luminous object. Observation time: 2 to 3 minutes
description: On February 13, 1979, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness and their children observed a large white sphere moving across the sky at low altitude from west to east. This round, very bright object had numerous lights that shimmered from within. Three lights (yellow, green, and red) flashed beneath the object. Despite observing it for two to three minutes, the witness was unable to identify it. During the investigation, other testimonies of similar sightings were collected: since December 1978, the passage of a white sphere moving in the same direction had been noted. Witnesses also reported regular voltage drops in the area. The cause was never determined. Another witness stated that on December 4, 1978, at approximately 6:00 PM, they saw a trapezoidal object with a rectangular base. This object hovered at low altitude and was illuminated by red lights. The noise it emitted resembled that of a helicopter. The hypothesis of a light aircraft flying in this valley was raised, but the air traffic control center did not detect any aircraft on its surveillance and control radars at the indicated dates and times. The presence of airfields in the region and the repetitive nature of the sightings suggest that a number of them correspond to aircraft. However, the available information does not allow for confirmation of this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On December 3, 1978, between 5 and 6 a.m., three people observed a bright light illuminating the ground of a pasture. Flashing red and blue lights were also seen. The police found no traces or objects at the site of the phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the silent and rapid passage of a green glow and a droplet-shaped phenomenon: high probability of observing an atmospheric reentry but lack of precision (date).
description: Recent testimony (2015) of an earlier observation (date arbitrary). In December 1978 (the witness does not recall the exact date), around 6:40 PM, a bus driver observed a silent, north-south passage of a luminous phenomenon in the eastern sky. The UAP was described as a green glow, a sort of large water droplet followed by three smaller droplets. The passengers also observed the phenomenon. The entire thing disappeared with lightning speed. Only one witness account was collected. This account has all the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry of space debris: duration, appearance, and behavior. GEIPAN searched for other similar events in December 1978. On December 2, 1978, starting at 5:15 PM, a particular luminous phenomenon was observed from various points across France. An incident involving a military rocket launched from the Biscarosse test center is the cause of these observations. This rocket, which went into a spin during launch, was intercepted and exploded in flight at an altitude of 10,000 meters, which explains why this event was seen over part of France. Aside from the time discrepancy (5:15 PM versus 6:40 PM in this case), the discrepancy in the direction of observation is also unreliable: the witness was looking east, and the phenomenon was observed moving from north to south; to see the Biscarosse incident, the witness would have had to look west. Therefore, this is not the phenomenon the witness observed. The witness cites an article from the newspaper "La Provence" which discusses the observation of atmospheric reentry of rocket or satellite debris. It is quite possible that this is the phenomenon observed by our witness, but GEIPAN has not been able to find this article online. A search of the newspaper could clear up any doubt. The Spacetrack website (US Space Command) indicates numerous atmospheric re-entries of space debris in December 1978; the lack of a date in this testimony makes it impossible to search for possible correlations between the observation and one of these re-entries. Despite the resemblance to an observed atmospheric re-entry of space debris, GEIPAN cannot confirm this hypothesis due to a lack of corroborating information (the article in "La Provence" might provide the necessary details). Pending further information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to the lack of precise date information.

summary: Observation of rapid movements of a luminous object.
description: On November 25, 1978, between 3:30 and 3:45 PM, a witness at his workplace was intrigued by a stationary object in the cloudy sky. This rectangular-shaped object emitted a very bright light. This witness and a colleague observed the object moving at very high speed and in opposite directions on two separate occasions. The control tower at Limoges-Bellegarde Airport confirmed the flights of two aircraft in the area between 3:20 and 4:14 PM. The available information on these distant observations does not allow for an analysis of the observed object.

summary: Observation of a circular, red luminous phenomenon rising on the horizon: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Among its publications are older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case (formerly known as Saint-Calais (72) after the gendarmerie) is classified as type C by GEPAN. On November 21, 1978, shortly after 6:15 a.m., two people observed a circular, red luminous phenomenon rising on the horizon. This phenomenon moved slowly and then diminished. The gendarmerie, dispatched to the scene at 8 a.m., concluded that it was an astronomical observation of Venus; this was not confirmed by GEIPAN until 2013, due to doubt about the precise time of observation because Venus did not rise that day until 6:29 a.m.

summary: Observation of the variable speed movements of a colored luminous ball.
description: On November 18, 19, and 21, 1978, two people observed, near Mount Cimon and at different times, the movement of a luminous, violet-tinted sphere at varying speeds. No sound was heard. One of the observations lasted approximately three minutes before the phenomenon disappeared at very high speed.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 15, 1978, between 2:30 and 3:30 PM, several people observed a luminous object moving southwest to northeast. It may have fallen into the lagoon, but the exact location of the fall was not specified. Divers, special correspondents for the local newspaper, searched for the object but were unsuccessful.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On November 14, 1978, at 10:14 PM, a witness observed the rapid passage of a bright ball from southeast to northwest, followed by a fiery-colored trail. No sound was heard during the approximately fifteen-second observation. This person witnessed a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: Possible observations of an atmospheric reentry.
description: On the morning of November 8, 1978, several witnesses in different regions observed a luminous phenomenon rapidly passing across the sky. According to their descriptions, this object was followed by a colored trail and moved along a downward trajectory. The presumed impact sites were searched, but no traces were found on the ground. These witnesses likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous object.
description: On November 6, 1978, at approximately 7:30 a.m., three people observed the slow movement of a luminous object that intrigued them. No sound was heard during the observation of this orange object. The gendarmerie, contacted that afternoon, was unable to make any findings. No other witness statements were collected by the gendarmerie regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack further details.

summary: Observation of red glows in the night preceded by a whistling sound.
description: On October 30, 1978, around 2:30 a.m., two campers, half-asleep, heard a whistling sound and then observed a red glow from inside their tent for 15 to 20 seconds. At the same time, they felt the ground warming up. An hour later, the campers, unaccustomed to the nighttime noises of the countryside, heard another whistling sound. The young women did not look outside their tent. At daybreak, they noticed a burnt area on the ground a little further away and suspected that a vehicle might have been parked there. The police investigation found no other witnesses who had heard these suspicious noises or seen the glow. However, one witness claimed to have burned wood a year earlier in that same spot, wood that had been cleared from the hedge and embankment bordering the meadow: two other similar locations were found extending from the hedge. Around midnight, the campers tried to start a fire with damp twigs and toilet paper: the paper smoldered completely rather than catching fire. It is likely that during the night, a gust of wind caused the paper and the grass to ignite suddenly, giving off a glow for 15 to 20 seconds and creating a sensation of heat. The fire was located between the tent and the presumed parking spot of the vehicle.

summary: Observations of the movement of a luminous object in the sky.
description: On November 2, 1978, between 6:45 p.m. and 7:30 p.m., several people in the Loire and Haute-Loire departments observed the movement of a luminous object composed of several lights of different colors. Despite discrepancies in the accounts, all the witnesses were intrigued by the absence of any sound emanating from this object. Despite the police investigation, too little information was gathered to substantiate any hypothesis.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 28, 1978, at approximately 7:10 PM, several witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon rapidly moving from east to west across the sky. They described a fireball with a luminous trail on a horizontal trajectory. No sound was heard during the observation. The phenomenon suddenly disappeared. Based on their descriptions, these individuals likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the movement of a disc-shaped object.
description: On October 23, 1978, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness, accompanied by his frightened dog, observed for several minutes the movements of a luminous object emitting an orange light. Round in shape, the shimmering object changed speed and direction without the witness hearing any unusual noise. A fireball was seen emerging from the object. The object then suddenly disappeared. No other statements were collected by the police to corroborate the information provided by this single witness.

summary: Observation of an object in hovering flight.
description: On October 15, 1978, at approximately 6:50 PM, several people in a vehicle observed two lights and a steady red light above the trees at the roadside. Continuing on their way, they saw an object with several lights, the shape of which was indistinct. No unusual noise was heard during the observation of the object, which appeared to be stationary at an altitude of approximately 150 meters. By the time they pulled over for a better look, the object had disappeared, leaving only a faint red light visible for a few moments. The object vanished silently and without smoke, heading west. A passenger in another car later reported seeing a strange flying object on the same day and on the same road between 6:30 PM and 6:45 PM. No further details were gathered regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observations of the passage of an elongated object across the sky.
description: On October 13th, around 8 PM, two witnesses in Troyes and Reims observed the passage of an elongated object. Colored lights were also seen. One of the two witnesses made a similar observation on October 18th between 7 PM and 8 PM. No abnormal phenomena were detected at the Aube satellite detection center. The technical department of the Barberey-Saint-Sulpice aerodrome informed the gendarmerie that no unusual sightings had been reported for those days. No other testimonies were collected. These witnesses likely observed the passage of an aircraft.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena.
description: On the afternoons of October 12 and 13, 1978, a motorist reported observing luminous phenomena moving across the sky. No noise was heard during the observations. No other accounts were collected regarding these phenomena, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a stationary red luminous sphere in the sky: observation of the Moon at its setting.
description: This observation was classified as a Category C case in 2010 by GEIPAN. It was the subject of a new investigation (see the document: investigation notes). On October 8, 1978, at 10:20 PM, two witnesses observed a luminous, fire-colored, stationary sphere above the fields opposite their home. An incomplete red circle surrounded the object. The phenomenon, with its variable brightness, lasted about ten minutes and then gradually disappeared into the night. No noise was heard during the observation or the disappearance of the phenomenon. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: the Moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was indeed visible in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness did not mention it. It is not the witness's visual perception that is the issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a minor anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the moon at sunset.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon related to the Moon.
description: On October 6, 1978, two witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon for 15 minutes that they could not explain. They described an unusual pink glow moving slowly about 7 to 8 meters above the ground. No noise was heard during the observation. The gendarmes, who arrived quickly on the scene, were unable to confirm the phenomenon, which had disappeared. No further sightings of this phenomenon were reported. The transition from woodland to cultivated fields is conducive to atmospheric turbulence of a thermal nature, causing distortion of the observed object. At the time and in the direction indicated that evening, these individuals likely observed this type of phenomenon in connection with the setting of the moon, which was then in its first quarter and very low on the horizon.

summary: Observation of a cigar-shaped object with an effect on a vehicle.
description: On October 3, 1978, around 2:00 a.m., a person on a moped was startled by a bright light above a wooded area. The witness then saw a cigar-shaped object, reddish-orange in color and encircled by a bright green ring. This object, motionless 100 meters in the sky, blinded the witness. The moped stopped running. The object disappeared abruptly, accompanied by a faint buzzing sound. The moped then started again, allowing the frightened witness to continue on his way. Another person reported seeing this type of craft again in the area, without providing further details.

summary: Sighting of a round, bright object in the sky.
description: On September 30, 1978, at approximately 11:30 PM, two walkers observed a very low-flying object that intrigued them. The object was round, with a shiny body and red and yellow lights. No noise was heard during the object's rotations above a railway bridge. No other witness statements have been collected to corroborate this sighting, for which we lack further information.

summary: Observation of two luminous flying objects in the sky.
description: On September 27, 1978, at approximately 7:35 PM, a telephone call to the Sète signal station reported the presence of two stationary lights in the sky. The officer on duty confirmed the report, noting the presence of a first object cylindrical in shape with a bright, conical front and a second crescent-shaped object that appeared and disappeared. The station chief was contacted and also confirmed the presence of these two objects. The objects disappeared behind clouds around 8:20 PM. The callers likely saw balloons.

summary: Observation of a luminous object in the sky.
description: On September 24, 1978, three people observed a luminous object in the sky that intrigued them. The silvery object made no sound and appeared to sway. It slowly disappeared, hidden by the landscape. These witnesses likely observed a balloon.

summary: Observation of a luminous streak passing across the sky.
description: On September 17, 1978, at approximately 7:50 PM, several people observed a luminous streak in the sky moving slowly at an unspecified altitude. No sound was heard during the observation. Despite the police investigation, the brief witness accounts concerning this phenomenon provide little information. The case is classified as Class C.

summary: Observing the movement of a luminous object in the sky.
description: On September 15, 1978, between 9 and 10 p.m., a witness in his garden observed a luminous flying object at a very high altitude, moving from west to east. The object was cigar-shaped and illuminated by white lights. No noise was heard during the observation. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: A block of ice fell.
description: On September 8, 1978, at approximately 7:15 PM, several people heard a whistling sound from the sky followed by a loud noise. A farmer later discovered that the roof of his barn had been damaged and found pieces of whitish ice of varying sizes. The sky was cloudy that day. The diameter and total weight of the iceberg could not be determined because it broke into several pieces. Some were collected by witnesses, and the rest melted on the ground without leaving any particular trace. No other similar events occurred in the region that day. This rare phenomenon is nevertheless known in meteorology.

summary: Successive observations of the passage of a satellite.
description: For several consecutive evenings around 9 p.m., people observed a luminous object passing at a very high altitude and constant speed. It moved in a NE-SW direction. The regularity of the trajectory, the duration of visibility, and the repetition over two days confirm the hypothesis that it was an observation of an artificial satellite.

summary: Probable observation of the maneuvers of a jet aircraft.
description: On September 4, 1978, around 10:00 PM, a group of people observed a luminous object in the sky that intrigued them. This white, spherical object was moving at the speed of an airplane on a north-south trajectory between the peaks in the area. After several minutes of observation, as an aircraft flying in the opposite direction approached, the object rose vertically and changed color before disappearing at high speed into the sky. The police investigation failed to gather any further information. The noise heard and the evasive maneuver of the second aircraft as it approached, with the activation of its standard identification lights, suggest that these witnesses likely saw maneuvers by a military jet.

summary: Observing the movement of a glow in the sky.
description: On September 1, 1978, at 9:05 PM, three members of the same family observed a red glow in the sky. It moved slowly between Mont Saint-Michel and Mont Angel. The observation lasted two to three minutes. The gendarmes, contacted immediately by telephone, made no further observations. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On August 20, 1978, between approximately 10:50 PM and 11:15 PM, five soldiers observed an intriguing object hovering above a building. Initially, three bright points were seen coming from the east, flying in a constantly changing formation. Then, for two minutes, the points merged into a single orange light above the building. Finally, the object disappeared to the north, its trajectory punctuated by sudden stops and accelerations. It was lost from sight due to its distance. No noise was heard during the observation. The witnesses stated that they could not mistake this nighttime light for a star or a known aircraft. No other sightings were recorded in the area that night.

summary: Probable observation of a satellite.
description: On August 6, 1978, two people reported observing the slow movement of a luminous object in the sky. According to the witnesses, a very bright yellow light moved slowly and steadily for three-quarters of an hour at high altitude in a southeast-northwest direction before disappearing from their sight. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. These individuals likely observed the movement of a satellite.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of an orange luminous phenomenon; gradual disappearance: observations of the Blood Moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case study, previously classified as D and named CASTRES (81) 30.07.1978, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On the night of July 29-30, 1978, at approximately 3:45 a.m., a moped rider (T1) returning from a party in Castanet-le-Haut (34) spotted a huge orange glow in the sky while at a place called Le Deves, in the commune of Murat-sur-Vèbre. The UFO was also observed by another witness (T2) from the same location. The observation lasted five minutes, after which the UFO disappeared at moderate speed. A gendarmerie patrol was informed of the case on August 1, 1978. The two witnesses were immediately questioned. The on-site investigation did not uncover any other witnesses or any traces on the ground. The direction indicated by the two witnesses corresponds precisely (within one or two degrees) to that of the Moon (see the investigation report). The reddish moon at sunrise or sunset is the source of many misinterpretations by witnesses (see GEIPAN records at www.geipan.fr, search for cases involving lunar phenomena). It is generally the presence of clouds in front of the moon that creates the confusion; they obscure it sufficiently to make it unrecognizable, yet still allow its glow to show through gaps that can take on all sorts of shapes, some of them strange. The complex shape indicated by witness T1 (disc and domes) could be one of these. Weather information still available 40 years later neither confirms nor denies such a cloud configuration. The swaying movements of the UFO can be explained by a perceptual error linked to the movements of cloud formations in front of and around the moon. The final rightward movement of the UFO observed by T1 necessitated contact with the witness. T1 spontaneously mentions what still seems strangest to him: the moon suddenly disappeared, and when asked, "Which way was it?" he answers, "Forward," "Ahead of me." He remembers seeing it move away. When reminded of his testimony of movement to the right, he replies that there was some movement, but it was mostly forward. T1 was therefore a victim of the classic perceptual error of interpreting a change in the intensity of the UFO (here, its decrease due to the closing of the cloud cover) as a change in the distance of the UFO, in this case, a movement away. This point illustrates once again that the witnesses' statements should not be taken literally, as they also contain interpretations. The very high degree of consistency between the true position of the Moon and the position of the UFO leaves no doubt about the misunderstanding. This case is consistent (2 independent witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. It is not the witnesses' visual perception that is in question, but rather their interpretation of their observation of the unrecognized phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the Blood Moon.

summary: Observation of the fall of a luminous object.
description: On July 27, 1978, at approximately 11:30 PM, several witnesses observed a bright red ball emitting a very intense glow. It appeared to fall from the sky near their homes. One of the witnesses reported seeing the ball rise again at 12:45 AM and then fall away. Neither the witnesses nor the police found any trace of the object falling in the area. No further information about this phenomenon was gathered.

summary: Astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On July 22, 1978, at approximately 11:45 PM, several people observed a very bright, yellow-orange light emitting beams in the sky. For 15 minutes, one witness observed the phenomenon through binoculars before it disappeared. Given the direction of observation and the position of Venus, which was particularly visible at that time of year, it can be said that the witnesses made an astronomical observation.

summary: Brief observation of a stationary luminous orange object in the shape of an upside-down plate: probable observation of the Moon.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. This observation, previously classified as D and named PRECY SOUS THIL (21) 18.07.1978, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. Around 4:00 AM on the night of July 17-18, 1978, a camper observed a stationary luminous phenomenon in the sky at a low altitude. The witness described an orange sphere shaped like a saucer or an inverted plate. The witness took three photographs before the phenomenon slowly, then rapidly, disappeared to the south. No noise was heard during the observation. The gendarmerie collected no other witness statements in the surrounding area regarding this phenomenon, and developing the photographs yielded nothing. The color of the UFO (fire, therefore orange), as well as the fact that it was low on the horizon, towards the southwest, is entirely characteristic of a setting celestial body (see the investigation notes). If we momentarily disregard the description of its final southward movement, we have a solid explanation for the UFO. Indeed, the Moon is present (verified by Stellarium) at an azimuth of 240°, which is precisely the direction of Dompierre-en-Morvan (as seen by the witness from Lucenay, approximately 240°), a direction attributed to the initial phase of the UFO. The hypothesis of a misidentification with the Moon would be reinforced by the fact that its angular altitude of 2° is perfectly consistent with a description of a low-altitude UFO of a fire color (the color of a reddish-brown moon at sunset). Furthermore, clouds were forming at that time. A portion of the Moon visible through breaks in the clouds can take on any shape, including the one described by the witness. The final southward movement is poorly documented. It remains consistent with the Moon misinterpretation, given that the break in the clouds could have moved southward, or at least appeared to move southward when observed from a bearing of 240°. However, the wind was generally easterly that day (no information available at 4:00 AM) and could indeed be broken down for the witness into a radial movement of approach from the bearing of 240° (not perceptible to the witness) and a movement perpendicular to the bearing of 240°, which was perceived as southward. The very high degree of consistency between the Moon's actual position and the position and description of the UFO lends considerable weight to the lunar explanation, and the limited information available about the UFO's final trajectory remains compatible with this explanation. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (fatigue, astonishment). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UFO B, a probable observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Moon.

summary: Brief observation of the presence and rapid disappearance of a fluorescent green disk in the sky; no noise: lack of information and cross-checks for this old observation reported in 2016.
description: Recent testimony (2016) of an earlier observation. On July 17, 1978, at 11:30 PM, several people in a farmyard observed a perfectly round, fluorescent green disc, motionless, above the house. The phenomenon disappeared with lightning speed. Only one witness account was recorded. This three-second observation of a green disc disappearing at lightning speed has certain characteristics of a bolide (atmospheric re-entry of a meteorite). The initial stillness of the observation is surprising for this hypothesis, but if the phenomenon is viewed almost head-on, the witness may have the illusion of stillness. The apparent change of direction could also be a consequence of the relative geometry of the phenomenon with respect to the witness. Nevertheless, this observation is notably different from other bolide observations: no luminous trail was observed. Furthermore, no other observations of this type appear to have been recorded, which is surprising for a phenomenon of this kind. GEIPAN received this observation report in 2016; beyond these basic checks, GEIPAN cannot conduct a more in-depth investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the passage of a flying object.
description: On July 8, 1978, at approximately 11:40 PM, a witness observed a north-south passage of an elongated flying object. Located at an altitude of between 1000 and 2000 meters, the witness estimated it to be composed of four non-radiating red spheres. No sound was heard during the brief observation. No other reports have been collected regarding this case, for which we lack information.

summary: Probable observation of a meteorological phenomenon.
description: On June 19, 1978, between 11:00 PM and 12:45 AM, several people heard a loud, muffled noise and then observed a luminous object above the town. The object was orange and oval-shaped. Malfunctions in the street lighting were observed as the object moved across the sky. It gradually disappeared from the witnesses' view as it gained altitude. Furthermore, motorists on the RN113 highway towards Bordeaux, near La Réole, also observed a luminous phenomenon moving slowly across the stormy sky. The investigation by the gendarmerie and GEPAN (Groupe d'Études et de Recherches Astronomiques de Paris - French National Geological Survey) was unable to clearly establish a correlation between these two observations due to a lack of details and information. The witnesses likely observed a meteorological phenomenon related to the stormy weather threatening the area.

summary: Probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On August 15, 1978, between 9:00 PM and 9:10 PM, several witnesses in the Gard and Ardèche departments observed a reddish luminous phenomenon moving from southwest to northeast. The witnesses described an incandescent ball followed by a trail. No sound was heard during the observation. These individuals witnessed what was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of the movement of a UFO.
description: On June 7, 1978, between 7:30 and 8:00 PM, three fishermen aboard a boat observed a luminous phenomenon that intrigued them for several minutes. A white light moved slowly along the coastline and then approached them. Upon reaching them, the witnesses reported seeing a craft with colored flames emerging from the rear without any noise. Making a sudden change of direction to head back towards the coast, it vanished abruptly, leaving the witnesses very impressed. Other witnesses reported a similar sighting that same evening, but according to the description given to the police, it was probably a shooting star. The investigation determined that the fishermen's observation could not have been an airplane, a boat, a weather balloon, or signal lights. Despite a thorough investigation, this case remains unsolved.

summary: observations of luminous phenomena in the sky.
description: On June 7, 1978, at approximately 8:55 PM, a driver and his passenger observed a bright point of light in the distance (about 5 km away), which intrigued them. At 9:15 PM, a luminous, orange, oscillating disc began its slow, vertical ascent and disappeared into the clouds. Only a colored trail remained visible. Following the publication of this observation in the press, another person reported seeing a circular, yellow-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky on the same date, between 9:30 PM and 9:45 PM. These observations remain unexplained due to a lack of detail.

summary: Probable sighting of a weather balloon.
description: On June 4, 1978, between 8 and 10 p.m., numerous people observed the passage of a very bright, spherical object. This object moved oscillating from east to west. A darker mass was sometimes visible beneath the object. All these people likely witnessed the passage of a weather balloon, brightly illuminated by the sun, along with the meteorological probe placed beneath it. The meteorological centers in Rennes and Guipavas frequently launch this type of object in the region.

summary: Probable observation of a lenticular cloud.
description: On May 28, 1978, at approximately 9:00 AM, a witness observed a series of halos of different colors emanating from rays of light in the direction of the rising sun. The observation lasted between 6 and 10 minutes, after which the phenomenon disappeared. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been recorded. This person likely observed a lenticular cloud.

summary: Observation of several glimmers of various colours.
description: On May 26, 1978, between 2:00 and 2:15 AM, a witness observed several lights of varying colors moving above his village from his home. These lights ceased as soon as a vehicle passed through the village. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack details.

summary: Observation of a sphere and a beam of light.
description: On May 22, 1978, at approximately 12:15 a.m., a motorist and his passengers spotted a very bright, silvery-white sphere in the sky. Witnesses reported that a beam of light emanating from this sphere struck their vehicle on the rear left side. No damage was found to the vehicle. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected, and information about it remains scarce.

summary: Probable observation of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: On May 16, 1978, at 9:15 PM, two people observed a spherical object in the sky moving very rapidly in a north-northwest direction. This object was extremely bright. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. These witnesses likely observed a high-altitude aircraft illuminated by the sun.

summary: Probable observation of a satellite passing overhead.
description: On May 6, 1978, at approximately 10:50 PM, several people observed a luminous object that remained stationary in the sky for several minutes. Spherical in shape and orange in color, it exhibited irregular brightness. It disappeared, moving silently along a south-northwest trajectory. These individuals likely witnessed the passage of a satellite.

summary: Probable observation of aircraft passing overhead.
description: On May 5, 1978, between 10:45 p.m. and 11:15 p.m., three people observed an aircraft passing approximately 50 meters above them. No noise was heard, even though the aircraft was quite large. Lights of different colors were observed on the aircraft. At the time indicated by the witnesses, the gendarmerie investigation established that aircraft had made silent passes at Charles de Gaulle Airport while awaiting landing authorization. These individuals had likely witnessed similar aircraft passes.

summary: Observation of a slowly moving red glow. Sudden change of course.
description: On May 5, 1978, at approximately 7:30 PM, three people observed a red glow above an island. This glow moved slowly southward and then abruptly changed direction, heading northwest. No sound was heard during the observation, which lasted more than four minutes. The gendarmes observed the same phenomenon for one minute on May 12. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack precise details.

summary: observation by different witnesses of the descent of three fireballs. Disappearance behind the horizon line.
description: On April 30, 1978, at approximately 9:30 PM, several witnesses saw three fireballs. These disappeared behind the horizon, emitting a red glow. No sound was heard. No traces of this phenomenon have been found on the ground in the area, and we lack further information about it.

summary: OBSERVATION OF STRANGE LIGHTS IN THE SKY DURING A TRIP.
description: On April 29, 1978, while traveling in the Verdun region, a motorist and his passengers noticed a white glow in the sky around 2:30 a.m., which intrigued them. A large, triangular, reddish-orange luminous phenomenon then appeared, motionless in the sky. They stopped their vehicle, and no sound was heard during the observation. A white light then moved toward the frightened witnesses, who got back in their vehicle and continued on their way. No other reports concerning this phenomenon were collected.

summary: A large glow was observed on the horizon.
description: On April 29, 1978, at approximately 11:30 PM, several people observed a very long orange glow of varying intensity. This glow appeared to move from east to west at a low altitude. No trace of the phenomenon was found at the site of the apparition.

summary: observation of the movement of three bright red and flashing points.
description: On April 27, 1978, at approximately 10:00 PM, a motorist observed three flashing red lights about 100 meters above the ground. Initially unable to discern any precise shape from which these lights might originate, the witness noticed that they were moving slowly from east to west. A faint humming sound was also heard. During the observation, one of the lights descended closer to the ground and appeared to be shining a spotlight on it. The other two lights remained stationary. The witness then saw a dome illuminated with different colors. The local press reported other accounts of this unexplained phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a moving red dot in the sky and a weak radar echo lasting 7 minutes: unidentified, moderately strange phenomenon.
description: On Sunday, April 23, 1978, between 8:35 PM UTC and 8:51 PM UTC, following a telephone call, an operational duty officer at Air Base 105 in Évreux (27) observed a red light at an altitude between 10th and 15th degrees: its position was estimated to be in the 300° bearing of the Évreux base. The lookout personnel also observed the phenomenon, noting that its light intensity was decreasing. The officer requested radar assistance, which at 8:44 PM UTC recorded an echo in the 300° bearing of the station at a distance of 18 nautical miles and a movement towards 330° bearing at an estimated speed of 30 to 40 knots. Visual observations ceased at 8:51 PM UTC, and the radar was switched off. The officer wrote his report the following day, April 24, 1978. The radar observation report indicates the 24th as the observation date, but this error appears to be due to a typographical mistake. This allows us to validate the simultaneous occurrence of the visual observation and the radar trace, the recording of which we unfortunately do not have. It should be noted that the radar trace was very weak (1/5) but of long duration (7 minutes). Only one witness statement was collected. The GEPAN investigation rejected the helicopter and balloon hypotheses. It is surprising that the planet Venus, very visible that evening in a nearby position (azimuth 296th to 299th and elevation 4th to 1.5th), was not mentioned by the officer. Nevertheless, since the UFO's position was significantly different (azimuth 300th to 330th and elevation 10th to 15th), mistaking it for Venus seems extremely unlikely. The weak radar measurement, not confirmed by the other radar at Cinq-Mars-La-Pile, should be considered with caution. A false echo (e.g., secondary reflection) cannot be ruled out. GEIPAN classifies this case as D1: the phenomenon is moderately unusual and distant, but the witness testimony is fairly consistent.

summary: Observation of a white ball in the sky. Rapid movements.
description: On April 4, 1978, at approximately 2:45 a.m., a factory guard observed a white sphere five times above a state-owned forest. The sphere, of varying sizes, moved very quickly. It gradually disappeared into the sky. No other witness accounts or information have been gathered regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack details.

summary: Repeated observation of a large sphere.
description: On April 2, 1978, at approximately 11:35 PM, a driver and his passenger spotted a very bright yellow-orange glow. It appeared almost at ground level on the hillside. After stopping his vehicle, the witness observed a large hemisphere, the other half of which was hidden by trees. It moved from north to south without any sound being heard. The observation lasted approximately 50 minutes before the object disappeared as its brightness diminished. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a rectangular-shaped object emitting a dazzling light, sudden disappearance.
description: On March 24, 1978, at approximately 10:00 PM, a witness observed a dazzling scarlet light from their home. They then saw a rectangular object bathed in this light. Inside the object, the witness distinguished two yellow circles that could have been portholes. This object moved horizontally and then abruptly disappeared, leaving a faint pink glow behind it. No further information has been gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a round, luminous object in the sky: astronomical observation of the Moon at its setting.
description: This observation case was classified as C in 2008 by GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group). It was re-examined (see the document: investigation notes). On March 17, 1978, a witness observed a round, luminous object moving slowly in a south-northwest direction at around 1:30 a.m. No unusual noise was heard during the 10-minute observation, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. The object descended slowly toward the horizon. The police investigation did not uncover any new information regarding this phenomenon. This case is consistent, and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, brightness) with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: the moon at sunset. Furthermore, the Moon was clearly visible in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness did not mention it. The issue is not the witness's visual perception, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (fatigue, surprise). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as UAP A: an observation linked to a misinterpretation of the Moon at sunset, observed with partial cloud cover.

summary: Observation of an oval-shaped object, horizontal movement, no noise.
description: On March 16th, around 10 PM, witnesses spotted an oval-shaped object in the sky that shimmered, emitting red-orange colors. Coming from the northeast, it moved towards the southwest at low altitude and without making a sound. The object disappeared, hidden by the landscape.

summary: Observation of a luminous object with a change of trajectory.
description: On March 14, 1978, at approximately 7:30 PM, several people observed a luminous object of unusual shape in the sky. Two luminescent white spheres were connected by a red-orange bar. The object remained stationary for a moment before abruptly changing direction. The lights remained steady, and no change in intensity was observed. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of lights of various colours coming from a stationary object in a field in the shape of a "large inverted bowl" metallic blue grey and very bright: unusable as it exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website: www.geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as C due to a lack of information and named BONNIERES SUR SEINE (78) 1978, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On March 8, 1978, at 6:45 a.m., a motorist saw flashes of various colors through the woods, coming from a field. Upon reaching the field, she saw a very shiny, metallic gray-blue object shaped like a large, inverted bowl. Motionless and silent, it emitted flashing lights from its base. Frightened, the witness left after a minute but returned at noon with colleagues: a circular imprint was found in the ground at that spot. Alerted by public rumor the next day, the police contacted the witness and went to the site. No particular tracks were found, apart from those of a tractor. According to the witness, many curious onlookers had trampled the area. Preliminary note concerning a case where the testimonies and/or traces relate to a phenomenon explicitly described or observed on the ground: - in the absence of evidence that the ground phenomenon could only have arrived and/or departed by air, the search for an explanation exceeds the sole competence of GEIPAN, and a GEIPAN conclusion can only be formulated if proof or near-proof is established; otherwise, GEIPAN must conclude C: Unusable because it exceeds its sole competence. - conversely, the absence of testimonies or traces of phases where the phenomenon is above ground may lead GEIPAN to be unable to conclude due to a lack of reliable information (classic GEIPAN classification C). We are in the first scenario here, since nothing allows us to exclude the possibility that the phenomenon arrived or departed by ground. Examination of the traces in the field proves nothing either way. Consequently, GEIPAN class C: Unusable as it exceeds GEIPAN's sole competence. The analysis that GEIPAN can conduct within the limits of its competence and experience is as follows: - what is visually described is of moderate strangeness. - the visual description is consistent with the presence of a vehicle with lights in a field near the road before sunrise; the nighttime observation and the improbable nature of a vehicle at that time could have contributed to a misinterpretation. - the strangeness experienced in real time by the witness appears limited because, although he did stop (for only a minute), he did not wait for the phenomenon to develop. He did return to the scene, perhaps also prompted by his colleagues' reaction to his UFO hypothesis. However, the presence of a vehicle at that time is astonishing and constitutes the core of the strangeness. It could be linked to an illicit activity, although unverifiable, such as poaching. The observation is characterized above all by a lack of consistency in both the information and its reliability: - the main testimony, as well as the secondary testimonies of colleagues, were not spontaneous but given at the request of the gendarmerie; - the evolution or disappearance of the phenomenon was not observed; - the round or suspicious tracks were not noted by the gendarmerie; - the witness's perception of the unusual tracks may have been heightened by the perception of them, the collective frenzy (colleagues, journalists), and may have impacted certain aspects of their subsequent statement; - the non-spontaneous testimony of colleagues, concerning the minimally described and almost identical tracks, opens the possibility (unverifiable) of prior collusion or influence.

summary: Observation of bright points high in the sky.
description: On March 7, 1978, at approximately 7:15 PM, two witnesses on their terrace observed two overlapping red dots moving in a south-southeast direction. The observation lasted two minutes, then the dots suddenly disappeared. After a few seconds, a dot of the same size, emitting a white glow, appeared and moved at high speed toward the northeast. This observation lasted one minute. Another witness reported seeing a luminous point moving across the sky, but the time did not correspond to the first observation. No other accounts have been collected concerning this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a fiery red cigar-shaped object
description: On March 1, 1978, two witnesses in their vehicle spotted a luminous object in the sky around 6:30 PM, moving slowly in a south-south direction. The observation lasted 7 to 8 minutes. The object was long and large; it was primarily red in color. No unusual noise was heard. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the silent movement and disappearance of a luminous object.
description: On February 28, 1978, between 7:30 and 7:40 PM, a woman and her son spotted a very bright orange object moving rapidly across the sky from north to south. The observation lasted three minutes, during which no unusual noises were heard. The object stabilized, then slowly moved south before disappearing instantly. No trace of it was found at the scene. No further reports were collected about this unexplained phenomenon.

summary: Brief flashes of light observed. Probably a thunderstorm.
description: On February 26, 1978, at approximately 2:30 a.m., several people observed a bright, silvery shape in the sky. Witnesses described it as a luminous explosion. This phenomenon disappeared instantly; no sound was heard. That same night, police patrols observed lightning flashes originating from distant thunderstorms. These witnesses likely observed a luminous phenomenon stemming from this storm system.

summary: Multiple observations in France of the rapid passage of a luminous colored phenomenon: observations of a meteoroid reentry.
description: On February 21, 1978, between 8:45 PM and 9:00 PM, numerous witnesses in various French departments observed, for a few seconds, the rapid movement of lights of varying colors across the sky. The majority of witnesses described a roughly spherical object, about the size of a football, followed by a long, luminous trail, first green, then reddish-orange. Many witnesses reported a westward movement and a disappearance over the horizon or instantaneous. Seventy-eight sightings were recorded. The summary table of locations and times of observation (included in the investigation materials) is striking for its geographical extent and the corresponding time. This supports the theory of a unique phenomenon occurring at high altitude (> 50 km) and providing visibility over a wide area. This is a key characteristic of the well-known phenomenon of atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. This is supported by another key characteristic: the elongated glow and short duration. A longer duration could have also led to consideration of the related hypothesis of a spacecraft's atmospheric reentry. Nowadays, many sites record data collected on the ground (most often by automatic cameras) during these reentries, so reports to GEIPAN are resolved without specific investigation. The 2016 example with more than 20 recordings (included in the supplementary analysis IMO) illustrates the analogy with this earlier case of February 21, 1978, at 9 PM. The supplementary analysis contains a selection of witness descriptions that clearly convey the impression of rapid movement with a conical or elongated shape. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observations of a meteoroid reentry.

summary: Observation of a glow following the SNCF railway line.
description: On February 19, 1978, at approximately 4:30 a.m., two witnesses observed a glow moving along the SNCF railway line. This red and blue glow moved very quickly before disappearing. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the silent and high-speed movement of a luminous object followed by a trail and a second dull ovoid object; error in the date of the day: mistaking it for an artificial atmospheric reentry, involving the Cosmos 250 satellite.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. Among its publications are older cases, originally classified as type D, which are now being re-examined solely to improve the relevance of the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification in an investigation report. This case, formerly known as MONT LOUIS (66) 1978, is one of the recently revisited type D cases. On February 26, 1978, a witness reported to the gendarmerie an observation of a UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) on February 16 at 6:40 a.m., lasting one minute. While driving his truck on the RN 116 in the commune of Sauto (66), the witness spotted a luminous phenomenon ahead of him, above the Têt valley, which he could not explain. He stopped and got out of his vehicle. Initially stationary above the valley, horizontal to the witness's line of sight, the unidentified flying object (UFO) then moved off at very high speed towards the North-Northeast, without noise, passing directly over the witness. The UFO was then accompanied by a luminous trail, likened to that of fireworks. A second UFO, oval-shaped and medium-dark in color, followed the first. The investigation conducted on site by the gendarmerie failed to locate any other witnesses. No anomalies were detected on the EDF (French electricity company) network. No traces were found on the ground or vegetation in the surrounding area. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, trajectory) with a rare astronautical phenomenon: a satellite reentry. Furthermore, there was indeed a satellite reentry on the trajectory and at the time indicated, on February 15, 1978: that of Cosmos 250 (see the investigation notes). The meteorological data for February 15, 1978, are consistent with those of the witness, which is not the case for those of February 16, thus supporting the date error. The UFO's departure position is indicated in the police report as below the horizon, with a note stating that, according to the witness, this would not be consistent with an atmospheric reentry. However, the witness doesn't directly state that the UFO was below the horizon but seems to deduce it (e.g., "at the horizontal line of sight, therefore below the peaks of the surrounding mountains") by mainly remembering that it was at the horizontal line of sight, which is a rather imprecise notion. The perfect coherence between the UFO's trajectory, its timing, and that of Cosmos 250's atmospheric reentry on February 15, 1978, leaves no doubt about the misunderstanding. This case is moderately consistent (only one witness), and the description of the observed UFO is moderately precise. The witness's sincerity and credibility have never been questioned. However, due to the lateness of their testimony, they may have mistaken the observation date and misremembered the UFO's initial position relative to the horizon, which is perfectly understandable. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked with a misunderstanding involving an artificial atmospheric reentry, involving the Cosmos 250 satellite.

summary: Observation of an oval-shaped object, moving rapidly in a straight line
description: On February 14, 2008, and not February 23 as initially reported by witnesses, around 4:00 PM, several people observed a bright, oval object moving quickly across the sky on a straight trajectory. No noise or trail was observed. No further reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of a luminous, flat, oval-shaped, pale red object; sudden disappearance: observation linked to a misinterpretation with the planet Mars.
description: This observation is one of those previously published in GUITRES (33) on January 27, 1978. Following a report from a correspondent, GEIPAN consulted its archives and found a GEPAN investigation report on this case, concluding with a classification in Ae. On January 27, 1978, around 5:45 PM, a couple (T1 and T2) living in SAINT-CIERS-D'ABZAC (33) observed a strange object in the sky through their windows. The UFO, flat and oval in shape and reddish in color, appeared to hover in the direction of the town of GUITRES (33). After 4 or 5 minutes of observation, the UFO accelerated and then disappeared into the sky. The gendarmerie conducted an investigation on-site and in neighboring towns between January 29 and February 3, 1978. GEIPAN then commissioned two investigators from CNES who arrived on-site on April 12 and initially classified the event as D (unexplained), a classification that unfortunately remained in the GEIPAN database until the present document. The head of GEIPAN at the time subsequently supplemented the report with his own conclusion, classifying it as A; this supplementary report is a prime example of scientific ufology! This case is very consistent (three witnesses, one of whom is independent of the other two), and the description of the observed UFO is quite precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, color) with the planet Mars, which is very close to the indicated axis. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of average strangeness is classified as PAN A, an observation linked to a misunderstanding with the planet Mars.

summary: Probable sighting of an aircraft.
description: On January 25, 1978, at approximately 6:30 PM, seven children playing in the street observed an orange, oval-shaped craft flying overhead. Red and white lights, alternately flashing, were located at the base of the craft. Approaching from the south, it followed a curve to head west at the same altitude as light aircraft. The children's accounts differed regarding the noise they heard as the craft passed. No other witness accounts were collected concerning this possible aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On January 16, 1978, at approximately 6:10 PM, two witnesses observed a luminous, white-yellow, phosphorescent circular phenomenon for one minute. It moved at very high speed from north to south along a straight trajectory. During its movement, they noted that the object had a cylindrical shape with a red light, and then a luminous green color was visible at the front of the object. No sound was heard during its movement, but the phenomenon left a luminous trail. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observations of several silent luminous phenomena in the sky: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony (2011) of an earlier observation made on January 15, 1978, between 6:45 PM and 7:10 PM. Witnesses, driving on the D177 between Venasque and Gordes, made several successive observations of silent luminous phenomena that they could not explain and were very impressed by what they saw. The first observation corresponded to the planet Jupiter, due east (see astronomical chart). The testimony then corresponded to the characteristics of Thai lanterns: groups of luminous points, moving in the direction of the wind (southwest), and lasting for a few minutes. It should be noted, however, that the witness described white and red lights: even white lanterns emit a yellow-orange light. (Widely used in Thailand for festivals for centuries, these lanterns have become very common in France since the 2000s, but were rare at that time, used mainly by Asians and tourists returning from Asia.) It has not been verified that the movement of the lanterns was consistent with the wind (archives unavailable online). The other observations remain strange, but could be misinterpretations of the moon (half-moon due south), vehicles on the road, or the excitement of the second observation. However, this does not explain everything. This case is classified as "C": insufficient information to draw a conclusion, but one of the observations corresponds to Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of reddish-orange glows.
description: On January 14, 1978, between 5:57 and 6:45 a.m., several people observed, for a few seconds, bright red-orange lights illuminating the surrounding area. Two luminous orbs, one orange and one blue, were seen by a motorist 500 meters in front of his vehicle. We lack more precise information about this phenomenon.

summary: Observations of the slow movement of a luminous phenomenon of rectangular shape and red-orange color in the sky; presence of a halo on the long sides of the rectangle: observation of a solar column.
description: This case of observation was re-examined (see the Investigation Notes document). On January 13, 1978, at approximately 5:40 PM, a woman and then her husband observed the slow movement of a rectangular, reddish-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky; a halo was noted along the long sides of the rectangle. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. No traces were found on the ground, and no other statements were collected by the police regarding this phenomenon. This case is consistent (two witnesses), and the description of the observed UFO is precise. The sincerity and credibility of the witnesses have never been questioned. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color) with a luminous phenomenon linked to the Sun: a solar column. Furthermore, the Sun had just set below the horizon directly along the axis indicated by the witnesses. The winter season and the presence of some clouds facilitated the observation of a solar column. It is not the visual perception of the witnesses that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (astonishment, observation of a rare luminous phenomenon). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of a minor anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misinterpretation of a solar column.

summary: bright glow was observed, seemingly following the witness.
description: On January 7, 1978, at approximately 4:50 a.m., a witness riding a moped saw three very bright lights close to the ground. One of these very powerful lights detached from the group, approached the witness, and followed him to the entrance of the neighboring village before disappearing. No noise was heard. No helicopter flights were conducted in the area that night. This phenomenon has not been identified.

summary: Observation of a slowly moving object.
description: On January 1, 1978, at approximately 5:15 PM, a farmer observed a flashing orange light in the southwest sky. It moved slowly southward. The observation lasted two minutes. No other accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information.

summary: Observations of the silent movement of a spherical and blinking object in the sky.
description: On October 20, 1979, several people in the Vosges and Haut-Rhin regions observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that flashed irregularly. The spherical object appeared to move in a zigzag pattern, and no sound was heard. A similar phenomenon had been reported by witnesses a year earlier. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.
